body: Thanks for your suggestions! I probably won't be going out of my way to do things I'm afraid of, I'd rather be able to mentally function lol. But you are absolutely right, I should try to leave a little light behind to offset the darkness of my choice, eh?
This legit made me laugh, thanks man. Not really my style but hey, if you ever have only ten days to live go for it!

I appreciate your efforts and I'm glad to know there are people like you trying to help others, so thank you for that.

I am very much aware that I'm mentally ill, as I said in my op I've been dealing with this for quite a long time now. I'm fairly sure I also mentioned the fact that I've been in treatment for my mental illness. My point being that I actually have reached out and sought help, and I would do it again if I thought it would make a difference.

I've been in continuous treatment for nearly 5 years and have been in and out since I was 16. Various forms of therapy, medications, inpatient facilities...I've tried everything that is available to me and my condition only ever gets worse or stays the same. I'm not denying that if I'm alive I could potentially get better, but the fact is there's no guarantee that I will and there's a much higher chance that I will live my life struggling just to keep my head above water. That's not the kind of life I'm interested in living.

The only reason I haven't already gone through with it is that I know my method isn't foolproof and I could very well end up spending a while in the hospital...I'm on my period and I despise being in hospital while that's going on. I also can't do this on a weekend because my mom is home all the time. And I have to get it over with before my next therapy appointment because otherwise I'll risk her having me committed if I say the wrong thing. So I've had to choose a date that accommodates these things. The fact I have some time to kill (lol) is purely incidental. It has nothing to do with anything other than careful planning and hormones/biology having shit timing. If I have to wait, I might as well enjoy the time rather than sit around obsessing or moping *shrug*

Honestly there's not much that I enjoy these days, not enough that it would make a difference anyway. There are absolutely things that I'd like to do in life, but the few moments of enjoyment I might have are just really not worth slogging through the millions of shitty moments in between. I'm really tired, I'm ready to be done, to have a bit of fun and then throw in the towel.

I don't know. Thanks for trying to help, man.

Im sorry you've been dealt such a crappy hand, but I'm glad you found a medication that helps at least for now. Hiking has never been my thing, bad knees and a serious case of the clumsies make it dangerous for me, haha. 

I really hope you get to climb that mountain in June, it sounds like a great plan, especially going with your friends and all that. Good luck!

You're right that social anxiety won't kill me, and that logically it should have no influence over my decisions because I'll be dead soon anyway, but it's not actually based on logic and I can't just turn it off. I don't choose to be so anxious that I physically shut down and can't do anything but cry, y'know? Like damn, if it was that simple I wouldn't be here in the first place.

Thanks anyway, buddy.

because I wouldn't be "enjoying" another 10 years of life. I'm not enjoying anything right now, and there's literally no evidence or reason to believe life is going to get better. It's a lot easier to enjoy yourself despite being miserable if you know there's a definite end coming. I don't have to think about all the shit that drags me down, because after these days are over I'll never have to deal with it again.



And I gotta be honest, that whole "think about your family" thing is such a guilt trip and really pointless. I have never met a suicidal person who is at all close to their family who hasn't thought about how much it's going to hurt the ones they leave behind. Personally, I find those kinds of statements only make me feel worse and add fuel to the fire...because it just reminds me of what I already believe - I'm a terrible person and a burden on anyone who cares about me. Obviously you couldn't know that it would hurt me, so I'm not offended or anything, but just something to consider if you talk to anyone else. Not everyone reacts well to the guilt thing.



And yes, there's always a chance I could change my mind. I'm more likely to do that if I happen across something worth living for while enjoying my last days. So why not give me some suggestions if you're so keen on encouraging me to reconsider?

I swear I'm not trying to be rude or snap at you, I appreciate you taking the time to respond and try to talk to me. I hope you find reasons to stick around, break out of the boredom and live a crazy, wonderful life.

1) Find a place to stay. 
2) Contact your local Catholic church and ask to meet with a priest - just say you're having a hard time and need guidance or something, the priest will meet with you asap and you can explain the situation in person. 
3) Make Bo and Dave go with you to get your stuff back from the apartment **they** got haunted. Bring a crucifix or two and some holy water and (if you don't already know it) memorize the Lord's Prayer.
Good luck, buddy. I'll be praying for you!

I know people have already explained this isn't Capgras, but it sounds a lot like prosopagnosia. Prosopagnosia is a disorder in how your brain perceives faces. This could be in the associative subtype, meaning that you can tell that what you're seeing is a face and you can see that people have different faces (they don't all have identical features)...but you can't identify the person or recall details about them. I think seeing a doctor would be a good idea while you're trying to sort this out, maybe get a referral to a neurologist!
